items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: And George Mraz is George Mraz.

ctx.x: Well I used to work, okay I’ll get back to me chronologically. So after Tony Scott I started working with Kai Winding and J.J. Johnson. Kai and Jay. Very successful. The most successful commercial group I’d ever — he had some hit records. And the group was a great experience because it was very tightly organized. And I made about six albums with them. I’m still waiting for them to be on CD. We recorded for Columbia with Paul Chambers and Kenny Clarke and I was spoiled that way. Even now, like because I played…
We were talking about the group with J.J. and Kai.
